correctness.rationale: PASS: An n-regular connected bipartite child graph on m=2^{n-1} vertices has two equal color classes and a unique coloring up to reversal. For two bipartite children, a compatible cross matching chooses one of two relative orientations and independently permutes the m/2 vertices in each class, giving 2((m/2)!)^2 of m! matchings and p_n=2/binom(m,m/2). Since each child remains an induced subgraph, a nonbipartite child cannot become bipartite. The independent-child recursion squares B_{n-1}; duplicate-child recursion does not. Conditioning factorizes the child laws according to the relevant sampling model and makes each new orientation seed fair and independent of child content; raw permutations still depend on child bipartitions, as correctly stated. Stirling gives log p_k=-2^{k-1}log2+(k/2)log2+(log pi)/2+O(2^{-k}), producing both precise asymptotics; for finite connected n-regular graphs, -n spectral eigenvalue and period two exactly correspond to bipartiteness. Independent 24-permutation enumeration recovered the dimension-three probability, and exact symbolic products through n=6 match; these finite checks corroborate but do not prove the general recurrence.

originality.rationale: PASS (qualified): Benjamini–Dikstein–Gross–Zhukovskii 2024/2025 define both exact independence structures and discuss typical chromatic/nonbipartite behavior, spectral properties, and diameter. Their available full primary text notes that bipartiteness fails with high probability but does not state these exact rare-event products, separation of n2^n versus 2^n exponents, or conditional matching kernels. Baran–Šarković 2026 concerns typical random-walk mixing and nonbipartiteness, not full exceptional-event enumeration. General balanced-color matching count is elementary, but its repeated independent/duplicate recursion and quantitative comparison are the assessed theorem.
residual_risks: A different chromatic-number derivation in Baran–Šarković technical sections could contain a stronger exceptional-event result; original full text not retrieved.
The conditional orientation bit is independent only in the recursive conditional sampling representation, not that all original matching permutations become unconditionally independent.
